variables.reason: The ledger variable name Ra and its physical definition (“First-order absolute moment (mean absolute deviation) of surface height fluctuations”) match the KB entry pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness which lists symbols Ra and R_a and defines arithmetic mean roughness as the mean absolute deviation of surface height. That KB entry explicitly reports si_dimension: L and a dimension_vector with the length coordinate set (supporting a single nonzero length exponent). pq_mean_roughness_height further documents the same dimensional class (mean roughness height, si_dimension L). Both cited records therefore justify the candidate exponent vector with L=1 and all other base exponents zero. Cited vectors supply the recorded length dimension and no other base dimensions, supporting all known coordinates of the proposed SI vector.

The ledger variable kt is defined as peak-to-valley height; the KB entry pq_peak_to_valley_height explicitly lists symbols including kt and defines it as a roughness amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences. That entry gives si_dimension: L (length). pq_mean_roughness_height corroborates the same dimensional character for surface-height measures. Together these records directly justify the candidate exponents with L=1 and all other base exponents zero.

The ledger variable k_rms is defined as root-mean-square roughness height; pq_rms_roughness_height in the KB lists symbols k_rms and krms and defines it as the RMS fluctuation of surface height about its mean with si_dimension: L. pq_mean_roughness_height provides an additional canonical length-class reference. These entries justify the candidate vector with L=1 and all other base exponents zero.

The ledger variable Sk is defined as the (third central) skewness of height fluctuations normalized by k_rms^3. The KB entry pq_height_skewness names symbol Sk, defines it as the third standardized moment, and explicitly records si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record directly supports all zero base exponents in the candidate vector for Sk.

The ledger variable Ku is defined as the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of height fluctuations. The KB entry pq_height_kurtosis lists symbol Ku, defines it as a fourth standardized moment, and reports si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This directly justifies the candidate all-zero SI exponent vector for Ku.

The ledger variable ES is defined as effective streamwise slope (rise over run). The KB entry pq_effective_surface_slope uses symbol ES, defines it as a mean absolute gradient (length divided by length) and explicitly records si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record supports the candidate all-zero SI exponent vector for ES.

The ledger variable Po is defined as surface porosity (a fraction). The KB entry pq_porosity lists symbol Po (and related symbols), defines porosity as a fraction of area/volume and records si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That authoritative entry directly supports the candidate all-zero SI exponent vector for Po.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The target nondimensional group is the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness ks/Ra; the provided independent variables include three length measures (Ra, kt, k_rms) and four dimensionless shape/structural descriptors (Sk, Ku, ES, Po). Dimensional analysis assigns length dimension to the height measures and dimensionless (all-zero exponents) to the normalized moments, slope and porosity, enabling construction of ks/Ra as a function of the listed dimensionless inputs.

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (mean absolute deviation) of surface height fluctuations (average absolute height above the mean).
Peak-to-valley height of the surface (maximum vertical distance between peaks and valleys in the profile).
Root-mean-square height of the surface roughness (square-root of the mean squared deviations of height).
Dimensionless skewness of height fluctuations (third central moment normalized by k_rms^3).
Dimensionless kurtosis of height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment).
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness (mean surface slope in the flow direction, rise over run).
Surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is void/open).

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (mean absolute deviation) of surface height fluctuations (average absolute height above the mean).
Peak-to-valley height of the surface (maximum vertical distance between peaks and valleys in the profile).
Root-mean-square height of the surface roughness (square-root of the mean squared deviations of height).
Dimensionless skewness of height fluctuations (third central moment normalized by k_rms^3).
Dimensionless kurtosis of height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment).
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness (mean surface slope in the flow direction, rise over run).
Surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is void/open).
